elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Amended 11.1 still obliges Customer to pay a "Termination for Convenience Fee" and amended 13.5 expressly characterises it as "the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer", so a Customer-payable liquidated amount survives.  The preferred (zero-LD) result is not reached; the drafter has deliberately taken the fallback.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The separate remaining-value "Termination for Cause Fee" in 11.2(A) is deleted and replaced by "the Termination for Convenience Fee", and 13.5 now reads "The Termination for Convenience Fee is Customer's sole early termination fee and is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement. No other amount payable by Customer under this Agreement shall be deemed liquidated damages or a penalty."  Retained items in 11.1/11.2(A) (unamortized Conversion costs, reasonable Expenses) are reimbursement of actual costs and are expressly de-characterised as liquidated damages by the new 13.5 sentence.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: 11.1 now reads "an early termination fee ("Termination for Convenience Fee") in an amount not to exceed three (3) months of Fees", replacing "REDACTED of the Estimated Remaining Value".  The cap is at, not above, the fallback threshold.  (Drafting note only: "three (3) months of Fees" does not identify the measuring period — consider "the average monthly Fees payable during the twelve (12) months preceding the Effective Date of Termination".)

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Amended 13.5: "...is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement. No other amount payable by Customer under this Agreement shall be deemed liquidated damages or a penalty."  The original acknowledgment that both fees were liquidated damages is removed, and no second liquidated formula remains.

elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Listed for completeness at the preferred level only; the retained Termination for Convenience Fee means the no-LD outcome is not achieved, which is why the fallback is the operative target.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the remaining-value percentage in 11.1 is replaced by a three-month Fees cap, the separate Termination for Cause Fee in 11.2(A) is folded into the same fee, and 13.5 confirms it is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
Preferred is correctly not claimed: a Customer-payable liquidated early-termination fee remains, so the finding is properly a deviation resolved at the fallback.

Minimality holds: edits are confined to the fee amount (11.1), the duplicate cause fee (11.2(A)) and the liquidated-damages characterisation (13.5). Deletion of "The Termination for Cause Fee shall not be subject to the limitations set forth in Section 13.4" is consequential (the defined term no longer exists) rather than cosmetic, and the unfavourable 13.4 carve-out for the Convenience Fee is left intact. Minor note: 13.5's second sentence largely restates the first; it could be dropped without weakening the element.

Intent defect to repair: the retained second sentence of 11.1 — "The Termination for Convenience Fee shall apply to any early termination of this Agreement other than pursuant to an Event of Default on the part of Customer or M&I" — now directly contradicts amended 11.2(A), which imposes that same fee precisely where M&I terminates following a Customer Event of Default. Fix in operative language, e.g. amend 11.1 to read "...other than pursuant to an Event of Default on the part of M&I or pursuant to Section 11.3 below, and shall also apply as provided in Section 11.2(A)", or open 11.2(A) with "Notwithstanding the second sentence of Section 11.1,".

Trigger-scope point worth flagging to the client (not a checklist element): as drafted, the three-month fee is still payable on any Customer Event of Default, however minor; consider requiring a material, uncured default if the walk-away concern (LD triggered by minor breaches) is to be fully closed.
Margin comment is accurate as to what changed and cites the accepted three-month fallback; it does not, however, disclose the 11.1/11.2(A) applicability conflict.
